findings.situation: A couple files jointly for 2025, but the spouse filed a separate 2024 return whose Form 4952 shows an amount on line 7, and the filer reads "Do you have ... your 2024 Form 4952" as asking only about their own return.
findings.source_text: f4952 p. 1, Part I, line 2: "Disallowed investment interest expense from 2024 Form 4952, line 7"
findings.why: The joint 2025 Form 4952 line 2 must include the spouse's 2024 carryforward. The gate explicitly says "by either of you, on a joint or separate return," but this question says only "you" and "your 2024 Form 4952" and never mentions the spouse, so the filer may truthfully answer no.

findings.situation: A filer's investment interest was first disallowed in 2022 and carried through 2024 Form 4952 lines 2 and 7 into 2025, and the filer is unsure whether that counts as "disallowed in 2024."
findings.source_text: f4952 p. 1, line 7: "Disallowed investment interest expense to be carried forward"; line 2: "Disallowed investment interest expense from 2024 Form 4952, line 7"
findings.why: "Investment interest expense that was disallowed in 2024" can be read as only interest first disallowed in 2024, which would exclude older carryforwards that 2024 line 7 includes. The parenthetical reference to line 7 points the other way. The two readings give different yes/no answers for line 2.

findings.situation: A filer whose only investment interest, or part of it, is reported on a Schedule K-1 from a partnership or S corporation reads the question as asking about interest they paid on their own loans, and leaves the K-1 amount out.
findings.source_text: f4952 p. 3, Line 1: "Include investment interest expense reported to you on Schedule K-1 from a partnership or an S corporation."
findings.why: The question asks only about interest on "a loan or the part of a loan" and never mentions K-1 amounts, so a truthful answer can leave out K-1 investment interest that line 1 must include. The gate lists K-1 interest, but the amount question does not ask for it.
